source.title: Rethinking Generalization in Reasoning SFT: A Conditional Analysis on Optimization, Data, and Model Capability
source.authors: Qi-Han Ren; Peng Wang; Rui-Kun Cai; Shuai Shao; Da-Di Guo; Yue-Jin Xie; Ya-Fu Li; Quan-Shi Zhang; Xia Hu; Jing Shao; Dong-Rui Liu

page_placements.theme: Reasoning safety and final-answer safety differ

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether benign SFT changes harmful-request compliance, using reasoning SFT and HEx-PHI ASR rather than the original fine-tuning setup. The safety experiments use pretrained base models, not safety-trained chat models.
record.gate_note: The study measures HEx-PHI attack success after Math-CoT and matched Math-NoCoT SFT. It does not test harmful-example fine-tuning, first-token KL, compliant prefills, suffixes, decoding changes, localized safety parameters, or methods to deepen safety. Results cited from other studies are not included.
record.test_reason: The safety experiment fine-tunes pretrained base models (Qwen3-14B/8B-Base, InternLM2.5-20B-Base) on benign math data and measures HEx-PHI ASR. The authors describe these as checkpoints 'before instruction tuning' with no alignment or preference optimization. V2 concerns benign fine-tuning eroding the safety of a safety-trained model, so these models are not the kind of system V2 names. The result, a rise in harmful compliance after benign reasoning SFT that is larger with long CoT, is close to V2 but sits outside it, so it is recorded under fits_no_version. No other version is touched: there is no harmful-example tuning, per-token KL, prefill or suffix attack, parameter localization, mechanism of shallowness, or deepening method. This call is borderline. If the panel treats the base models' native refusals (base ASR 20%) as 'safety', r2–r7 would bear on V2 as a T3 result.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that reasoning SFT generalizes conditionally and that long-CoT SFT weakens safety much more than matched no-CoT SFT, attributing this to procedural patterns rather than math content. The record's hedge needs one correction: the main text and related work claim a 'causal' attribution to procedural patterns, based on the matched CoT/no-CoT design. Only the self-rationalization correlations are explicitly called descriptive and non-causal (App. C.15).
record.recipe_differences: Uses standard SFT on 20k math reasoning examples, comparing long-CoT with matched no-CoT data. It starts from pretrained base models rather than aligned chat models and does not use a few-to-hundreds harmful or benign instruction examples.
record.method_sensitivity: Safety degradation is reported as substantially greater with long-CoT than matched no-CoT training; the study also reports model-specific ASR curves, but most plotted values are not stated numerically.

fits_no_version.finding: Benign math reasoning SFT of pretrained base models raises HEx-PHI ASR. For Qwen3-14B-Base it goes from 20.0% to 53.7% with long-CoT data versus 23.3% with matched no-CoT data. The text reports the same direction on Qwen3-8B-Base and InternLM2.5-20B-Base.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign long-CoT reasoning SFT of non-aligned base models increases harmful compliance, much more than matched no-CoT SFT.

fits_no_version.finding: Rule-detected self-rationalization occurs in 6.3% of base-model responses, 31.0% after NoCoT SFT and 67.3% after CoT SFT. Across CoT checkpoints it correlates with ASR (Pearson r=0.979); across NoCoT checkpoints it does not.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: After long-CoT SFT, harmful compliance co-occurs with in-reasoning self-rationalization.

record.problems: The safety experiments begin from pretrained base models, not safety-trained chat models. The exact ASR values for Qwen3-8B-Base and InternLM2.5-20B-Base are only plotted. Self-rationalization is detected with rule-based markers, which the authors note may have false positives or false negatives; they also state the correlations do not establish causality.
record.rows_left_out: No additional safety-related results meeting the row criteria were left out.

untested.parts: No safety-trained or chat model is fine-tuned; only pretrained base models. No ordinary instruction-tuning data and no data-size sweep.
No per-token KL between aligned and base models.
No prefill, suffix or decoding attacks.
No analysis of why alignment is shallow.

missing.what: Per-model ASR trajectories across checkpoints, plotted only, for all three models and both datasets.
missing.versions: none (would bear on V2 only if base models are counted)

missing.what: Mean ASR across checkpoint series: 44.8% for Math-CoT versus 24.7% for Math-NoCoT.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V2 'supports' and 'limits_scope' labels are removed because every safety subject is a pretrained base model, which has no safety training to erode. The Qwen3 base models do refuse often (base ASR 20%), which is why the exclusion is a judgment call; this is flagged in test_reason. HEx-PHI and its GPT-4.1 judge come from original source 2310.03693, but the study does not test that paper's finding on aligned models.

versions.untested_parts: No harmful-example fine-tuning or few-to-hundreds-example sweep.
Tests math reasoning SFT on pretrained base models, not safety-trained chat models or ordinary instruction-tuning datasets; no few-to-hundreds-example data-size sweep.
No per-token KL comparison between aligned and base models.
No compliant prefill, suffix attack, or decoding-change intervention.
No parameter or rank localization of safety behavior.
Does not test why safety would be shallow or how a training objective creates first-token concentration.
No training designed to deepen safety across response positions.

relation.reason: The study discusses reasoning-induced safety degradation without testing the supplied shallow-alignment versions on safety-trained starting models or using shallowness as a tool.

tranche.reason: The experiments start from pretrained checkpoints before instruction tuning, rather than establishing erosion of prior safety alignment. Self-rationalization is a related behavioral proxy; no other supplied version is tested.

source_check.notes: The listed values match Tables 15–16. The detector may yield false positives or negatives, and its checkpoint correlations are descriptive rather than evidence of an internal causal mechanism.
